summary: Frontend-only verification of the CSS visibility fix for native <select> options on the dark-themed 'Okul Hesapları' page. Because no general_admin credentials are available (test_credentials.md lists 'None yet'), I could not authenticate into /admin/school-accounts to visually count 15 district options. Instead, I verified the CSS rule is loaded globally by (a) reading /app/frontend/src/index.css, (b) inspecting document.styleSheets in the running app, and (c) injecting a probe <select><option> at runtime and reading getComputedStyle on the option. The rule `select option { background-color:#0f1629; color:#e2e8f0; }` is present in the stylesheet and getComputedStyle on an injected option returns bg=rgb(15,22,41) and color=rgb(226,232,240) — exactly matching the intended dark-theme values. The auth-gate redirect from /admin/school-accounts → /admin/login also works as expected.

critical_code_review_comments: Fix is minimal and correctly scoped to `select option` globally on the dark theme — appropriate solution. No dark-mode media query needed since the app is dark-only.
The rule will also apply to any future <select> across the app, which is desired and consistent with the base body colors (#0b1120 / #e2e8f0).

rca of the issue: Native <select> dropdowns render their popup at the OS layer using the option element's own background/color, not the styled <select>. On this dark theme, options inherited the browser default (white bg, and inherited light color from body) causing white-on-white invisibility for all options after the first (which was often OS-highlighted). Setting `select option { background-color:#0f1629; color:#e2e8f0; }` forces both explicitly so the native popup paints with dark bg + light text. Verified applied via getComputedStyle.
